---
title: "Quiz · Compose a Pico"
---

A short knowledge check. Answers are hidden behind callouts so you can
self-grade after answering.

## 1. In one sentence, what is **capability composition / resolution**, and how is it different from **rule compilation**?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
*Capability composition / resolution* takes one Pico definition and a
set of installed capsule definitions and produces a resolved
composition manifest that pins each `spec.capabilities` entry to a
specific capsule (memo2 §4 D4). *Rule compilation* is what
`bin/pico compose` does in this repository: it turns one parsed Rule
into one executable shell-script artefact and currently handles only
`kind: greeting` (verified in
[`memo24.md`](../../../../memo24.md) §2.4). The two operations live
in different repositories; the Academy ships neither resolver nor a
new validator (memo2 §4 D4 Consequences for the Academy).
See the [lesson](index.qmd#two-terms-kept-separate).
:::

## 2. Classify `foo.bar@0.1.0`, `foo.bar@1.2.0`, `foo.bar@=1.0.0`, and `foo.bar`.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
From memo2 §2 D2:

- `foo.bar@0.1.0` — **caret** (`0.x` variant). Resolves against any
  `foo.bar` capsule whose version has the **same minor** `1` and
  **patch ≥ 0**.
- `foo.bar@1.2.0` — **caret** on the `≥ 1.0` line. Same major (`1`)
  and version ≥ `1.2.0`.
- `foo.bar@=1.0.0` — **exact**. Strict equality on
  `metadata.version`.
- `foo.bar` — **bare**. Matches **any** version of a `foo.bar`
  provider.
:::

## 3. The lab's capsule provides `oe.greeting` at `0.1.0`. Why does `oe.greeting@=0.2.0` fail where `oe.greeting@0.1.0` succeeds?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
`@=0.2.0` is an **exact-match** constraint; it requires
`metadata.version == 0.2.0`. The installed capsule is at `0.1.0`, so
zero candidates survive the version check and the resolver returns
`outcome: error`, `error: no-matching-provider`,
`requirement: oe.greeting@=0.2.0`. `@0.1.0` is a **caret** constraint
on a `0.x` line; it requires the **same minor** and **patch ≥ 0**,
which `0.1.0` satisfies exactly — so the same capsule succeeds. See
the [exercise Task B](exercise.qmd#task-b-author-a-failing-pico) and
upstream fixture `fixtures/scenarios/exact-nomatch-patch.yaml`.
:::

## 4. Two installed capsules both provide `foo.bar` and both satisfy a Pico's bare `foo.bar` requirement. What does a conforming resolver emit at v0.1, and why can you not just pick one in `spec.composition`?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
It emits `outcome: error`, `error: multiple-matching-providers`,
`requirement: foo.bar`, and lists both candidate providers (upstream
fixture `fixtures/scenarios/duplicate-provider.yaml`). In v0.1,
*more than one* matching provider is an explicit error — memo2 §3 D3
§2 amendment: "resolving to more than one matching provider is an
explicit error (memo23 §5 rule 9 'Graceful failure')". The
`spec.composition` block that would let a Pico pick one is
**reserved for v0.2** and is upstream-owned; v0.1 Picos SHOULD NOT
declare it, and the Academy will not add such a block locally.
:::

## 5. A requirement reads `foo.bar@0.1.0` and the installed capsule is `foo.bar` at `0.2.0`. Does `0.x` caret cross a minor boundary?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
No. memo2 §2 D2 states explicitly that for `0.x` versions caret
requires the **same minor** and **patch ≥ requested**; a different
minor is a non-match. The resolver emits `outcome: error`,
`error: no-matching-provider`, `requirement: foo.bar@0.1.0`
(upstream fixture `fixtures/scenarios/zerox-different-minor-nomatch.yaml`).
Contrast this with the `≥ 1.0` line, where caret crosses *minor and
patch* within the same major (`fixtures/scenarios/caret-match.yaml`).
:::

## 6. Does `definitions/pico.yaml` need any change to teach Module 4, and where will capability composition be validated once the reference validator ships?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
No change is needed.
[`definitions/pico.yaml`](../../../../definitions/pico.yaml) already
requires `spec.capabilities: [string]`; each item is a capability
identifier (optionally plus a constraint) per memo2 §3 D3 §2
amendment. No new required field is added and the Academy does not
introduce `spec.composition` locally. Once memo2 §5 follow-up (b)
ships, capability composition is validated by the reference CLI in
`open-engineering-capsule/source`; the Academy MAY add a thin
delegating `pico resolve` wrapper that calls it. Until then,
resolution is done by hand against the upstream scenarios (memo2 §4
D4 Consequences for the Academy).
:::

## 7. Which capability identifiers below are grammar-conformant, and which are not? Give the memo2 §3 D3 reason for each rejection.

`oe.greeting`, `pico.state.set`, `Greeting`, `oe..greeting`,
`oe_greeting`, `github.issue.create`

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
Conformant: `oe.greeting`, `pico.state.set`, `github.issue.create` —
each is two or more dot-separated segments, every segment starts with
a lower-case ASCII letter, and only `[a-z0-9]` or single internal
hyphens appear.

Non-conformant:

- `Greeting` — upper-case leading letter *and* single segment (needs
  at least one `.`).
- `oe..greeting` — empty segment between the two dots.
- `oe_greeting` — underscore is not in the segment alphabet; also no
  dot separator.

See upstream fixtures `invalid/capability-upper-case.yaml`,
`invalid/capability-empty-segment.yaml`, and
`invalid/capability-underscore.yaml`.
:::
